solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American male in bar who can't relax on holiday?

definitions.note: short for 'one who can't relax on holiday', the noun the answer names

parts.note: b is the symbol for the bar, a unit of pressure
a man is a male

explanation.surface: A man from the States sits in a pub, apparently unable to unwind on his vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: A busman's holiday is a break spent doing much the same as your everyday work, as a bus driver might spend a day off riding buses; the question mark flags the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'busman's holiday' describes a vacation spent working, so the busman is the figure who never truly rests.

clue.text: Person who meddles by holding us, and then party, up

indicators.note: the word by holds the word us inside it

parts.note: 'by' is used again, this time holding DO, a party, written upwards as OD

explanation.surface: A meddler is someone who props up their party by roping us in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' does double duty: once around US and once around the reversed DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody is a nosy person who interferes in other people's business.

clue.text: Credulously believe insufficient evidence for climate change?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a story is to accept it uncritically
second meaning: a bird, since 'one ... doesn't make a summer'

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says one swallow does not make a summer, so a single sighting is too little evidence of the season changing.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to accept a tale without question, and the bird is the classic weak sign of summer.

clue.text: Share everything the writer found in parts of Bible

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: the writer's word sits within the two Testament abbreviations

parts.note: OT and NT, the Old and New Testaments
the writer of the clue refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: Someone finds a shared portion of everything in passages of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is one's allotted portion, a share given out.

clue.text: Way in Westminster political leader, bit by bit, gets followed by everyone

indicators.note: the leader is taken one letter at a time, so the word for everyone follows the first letter as well as the second

parts.note: PM, the Prime Minister
all means everyone
the leader's second letter is also followed by everyone, so the word all is used a second time at the end

explanation.surface: A Westminster politician, gradually, attracts a following from all quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: P and M are each followed by ALL, so the single 'everyone' serves both letters of the Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Pall Mall is a famous street in the City of Westminster, London, lined with gentlemen's clubs.

clue.text: As Republican president, I'll ban a monarch after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things upside down, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A Republican president vows to outlaw a monarch once the uprising is won.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln was the first US president from the Republican Party, elected in 1860.

clue.text: Contributor to world revolution? Set up first part of it

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: 'it' is the word revolution, whose first five letters are taken

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is told to begin the first stage of a global uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is that love makes the world go round, so a lover helps the world revolve.
explanation.definitionFit: One who loves contributes to love, which in the saying keeps the world turning.

clue.text: Largely outspoken, getting into trouble — kind of green

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: vocal means outspoken

explanation.surface: A mostly outspoken activist gets into trouble with the Greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks political; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocado is a dull yellowish-green shade named after the fruit's flesh.

clue.text: Old letter from innocent person to lawyer in US

parts.note: a lamb is a meek, innocent person
DA, a district attorney

explanation.surface: An old letter from a naive individual to an American attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests correspondence; it is an alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Editor's work, providing guidance on part of speech

parts.note: leading means guiding
an article such as a or the is a part of speech

explanation.surface: An editor's job described as giving direction on grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading article is a newspaper's editorial, the main opinion piece written by its editors.

clue.text: Short and stout, perhaps — it's of little significance

parts.note: short means small
stout is a dark beer, so it is an example of beer

explanation.surface: A description of a squat, plump figure, oddly dismissed as unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short and stout' reads as a body shape; stout is the drink, an example of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is an idiom for something trivial, of minor importance, from the old weak ale.

clue.text: Noise of engine in very restricted space

parts.note: a room is an enclosed, bounded space

explanation.surface: An engine roars inside a cramped little room.
explanation.definitionFit: Vroom is the imitative word for the roar of a revving motor.

clue.text: British on top of the world — certainly not before time

parts.note: the idiom for feeling elated

explanation.surface: A Briton feels on top of the world, though the success came far too late.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belated arrives late, which is the opposite of coming early or on schedule.

clue.text: Where some top Americans learn it's difficult bringing in a lot of change

indicators.note: the word for difficult takes the shortened word inside it

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to vary is to change

explanation.surface: A comment on how hard elite American students find adapting to change.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvard is the Ivy League university in Massachusetts, where many of America's elite are educated.

clue.text: Look for water to put out fire, say

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than spelt, matching another spelling

parts.note: to douse a fire is to extinguish it

explanation.surface: Hunting for water so as to extinguish a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound alike; one means quench, the other is the divining sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to search for underground water with a divining rod.

clue.text: Pardon me — that's not right way to make an impression

indicators.note: the letters are not set the right way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An apology for a social blunder in how one tries to impress others.
explanation.definitionFit: To name-drop is to mention famous acquaintances casually in order to impress listeners.

clue.text: Treatise is required in key academic programme

indicators.note: the word is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: D is a musical key
a course is a programme of study

explanation.surface: A treatise is required reading in a key academic course.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal written treatment of a subject, much like a treatise.

clue.text: Piece newspaper people put in daily, initially

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the daily's initials

parts.note: FT, the initials of the Financial Times, a daily paper
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
men means people

explanation.surface: Newspaper staff put a story into the daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a broken-off piece or part of something.

clue.text: Meat I got after parking a small vehicle

indicators.note: the I comes after the earlier pieces, so it is placed last in order

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone buys meat after finding a spot for their little car.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a seasoned, smoked beef, a cured meat of deli fame.

clue.text: In company of doctor, gripped by feelings of dread

indicators.note: the doctor is held inside the other word

parts.note: angst is anxiety or dread
MO, medical officer

explanation.surface: Someone in the doctor's company is gripped by dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Amongst means among, in the midst or company of others.

clue.text: Like judge in robes, switching sides

indicators.note: the letters at the two ends of the word trade places

explanation.surface: A judge in court dress, swapping allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first and last letters of robes swap; 'sides' are the word's two ends. The idiom is 'sober as a judge'.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile 'as sober as a judge' makes the answer the classic quality of a judge.

clue.text: Less able to see great performance in play

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an outstanding performance in a game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' reads like a theatre production; in British slang a blinder is a brilliant display, often in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of blind means having poorer sight, and the slang noun means a superb performance.

clue.text: Perfect state? Not really, but opiates, in part, can produce it

indicators.note: only part of these words is used, the answer lying inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of but and the start of opiates

explanation.surface: Drugs promise a perfect state that is only an illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined ideal society, a perfect state that does not really exist.

clue.text: Pondered hard about hot temperature

indicators.note: the word for hard goes around the letter for hot

parts.note: tough means hard

explanation.surface: Someone thought deeply about a hot temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Pondered and thought are synonyms, both past tense verbs for considering carefully.

clue.text: With moving air, suddenly band provides great enjoyment

parts.note: a gust is a sudden rush of moving air
a ring or band is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Wind blows suddenly as a band plays with zest.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment or relish in doing something.

clue.text: College heads approving preparation of courses

parts.note: the first two letters of College
OK-ing, giving the OK to something

explanation.surface: College principals sign off on the plans for new courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' looks academic beside 'College', but these are courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking is making food ready, and the courses here are the dishes of a meal.

clue.text: Contacts some workers in hotel and leaves

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., calls someone over a pager or speaker
second meaning: ..., the boys who run errands in a hotel
third meaning: ..., the leaves of a book

explanation.surface: Someone reaches some hotel staff and then departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb for departing; it is the noun, the sheets of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for summoning someone, a noun for hotel bellboys, and a noun for the leaves of a book.

clue.text: Poet using energy between pass and hilltop

indicators.note: between places the energy letter in the gap separating the pass and the hilltop

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a ridge is a long hilltop crest
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A poet draws on his energy while walking from a mountain pass up to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the poet was a great fell walker in the Lake District, so the surface pictures him on a hike.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Taylor Coleridge wrote The Rime of the Ancient Mariner and Kubla Khan, among English Romantic verse.

clue.text: Novel Thoreau finally had written

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order
only the last letter of had is used

explanation.surface: Thoreau finally had written a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book Thoreau wrote, but it signals new order.
explanation.definitionFit: To have authored something is to have written it as its creator.

clue.text: Feel bad about putting rook with another bird

parts.note: an egret is a heron-like wading bird, another bird beside the rook

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher is sorry to have grouped a rook with a different species.
explanation.walkthrough: The rook is a bird too, but R is its chess abbreviation, hence 'another bird' for the egret.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret something is to be sorry or remorseful about it.
